1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MWAA: Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow; SDK: software development kit; EMR: Elastic MapReduce; DAG: directed acyclic graph; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; NAT: network address translation; IAM: Identity and Access Management; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; ETL: extract, transform, load; RDS: Relational Database Service; CTAS: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT; AI: artificial intelligence; SQS: Simple Queue Service; SNS: Simple Notification Service; MV: materialized view; DLQ: dead-letter queue

  • Orchestrate pipelines with Amazon MWAA and AWS Step Functions and troubleshoot managed workflows
  • Call SDKs to use AWS features from code
  • Use Amazon EMR, Amazon Redshift and AWS Glue features to process data
  • Consume and maintain data APIs
  • Prepare data for transformation with AWS Glue DataBrew and SageMaker Unified Studio
  • Query data with Amazon Athena
  • Automate with AWS Lambda and manage events and schedulers with EventBridge

Orchestration design is in Module 4 and schedules and event triggers are in Module 1; this module is about running, automating and fixing them.

2Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows (skills 3.1.1 and 3.1.2)

Running case

Kestrel Freight Keeps the Pipeline Running

  • The nightly pipeline runs unattended and finishes at 05:00
  • Last night a DAG disappeared, a Step Functions run failed and a Glue job never started
  • The on-call engineer needs to know where to look
  • Your job: automate the runs and fix them fast
Service Where to look when it breaks Common causes
Amazon MWAA CloudWatch Logs for the scheduler, DAG processing, worker, webserver and task logs; the Airflow UI; the DAG files and requirements.txt in S3 DAG not showing: a syntax or import error, file not yet synced from S3, or a missing plugin or requirement; tasks stuck in queued: not enough workers (raise the maximum workers or the environment class); access denied: the execution role lacks permission; cannot reach the internet or a service: VPC route, NAT gateway or VPC endpoint missing
AWS Step Functions Execution history and graph view (which state failed and its input and output); CloudWatch Logs (needed for Express) States.TaskFailed (the service call failed), States.Timeout (task or heartbeat timed out), missing IAM permission on the execution role (especially for .sync and callback patterns), bad input path, no Retry or Catch
AWS Glue workflows The workflow graph (dynamic view), each job run's logs and error message, trigger state A trigger is not activated, a dependent job only runs if a trigger started the chain, workflow concurrency limit reached, job role or connection problem
EventBridge Rule metrics, dead-letter queue of a target, CloudTrail Event pattern does not match, target permission missing, target throttled
  • Automate recovery: Retry with backoff, Catch to a fallback state, alarms that notify, idempotent steps so a rerun from the failed step is safe
  • Operate: version DAGs and state machines, alarm on failure counts and duration, keep runbooks

Exam tip

"An Airflow task never starts and sits in queued" → add workers (raise max workers or environment class). "A Step Functions .sync task fails with access denied" → add the integrated service's permissions to the state machine role.

3Calling SDKs from Code (skill 3.1.3)

  • An AWS SDK (Python boto3, Java, JavaScript, Go and more) lets code call AWS services: start Glue jobs, run Athena queries, read S3, put Kinesis records
  • Credentials: never hard-code keys: run code with an IAM role (Lambda execution role, Glue job role, EC2 or task role); the SDK picks up temporary credentials automatically; secrets come from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store
  • Built-in resilience: the SDK retries with exponential backoff on throttling and server errors; tune maximum attempts and timeouts
  • Pagination: list and query calls return pages; use paginators or next-token loops
  • Waiters: poll until a resource reaches a state (for example an Athena query is SUCCEEDED)
  • Asynchronous calls: many data APIs start work and return an ID (Athena StartQueryExecution, Redshift Data API ExecuteStatement); poll the status (or use events) and then fetch results
  • Idempotency tokens (ClientToken) make retries safe for operations that create or change things
  • Region and endpoint settings, VPC endpoints for private access
Exam tip

"A Lambda function calls Athena and must wait for the query" → StartQueryExecution, then poll GetQueryExecution (or use Step Functions .sync) and read results with GetQueryResults.

4Using Service Features to Process Data (skill 3.1.4)

Service Features that automate processing
Amazon EMR Steps (a unit of work on a cluster), auto-termination of idle clusters, managed scaling, bootstrap actions, EMR Serverless (automatic capacity), notebooks (EMR Studio)
Amazon Redshift Stored procedures, scheduled queries (query editor schedules), materialized views with auto refresh, auto-copy from S3, Redshift Data API, zero-ETL integrations that replicate from Aurora, RDS and DynamoDB, streaming ingestion, automatic table optimization and concurrency scaling
AWS Glue Triggers and workflows, job bookmarks, auto scaling, Data Quality rules, Glue Studio visual ETL, interactive sessions, DynamicFrames, pushdown predicates, Flex execution
Amazon Athena CTAS and INSERT INTO for ETL, views, workgroups, federated queries, result reuse
  • Pick the built-in feature before custom code: it is cheaper to run and easier to maintain

5Consuming and Maintaining Data APIs (skill 3.1.5)

  • Consume an API: authenticate (IAM, tokens, keys in Secrets Manager), paginate, respect rate limits, retry on 429 and 5xx (Module 1)
  • Maintain an API you publish with Amazon API Gateway:
    • Stages (dev, test, prod) and deployments; version the API path or header; deprecate old versions gradually
    • Throttling and quotas (default 10,000 requests per second per account per Region with a burst) and usage plans with API keys
    • Caching of responses to protect the backend
    • Authorization: IAM, Amazon Cognito user pools, Lambda authorizers
    • Monitoring: CloudWatch metrics (4XX, 5XX, latency, count) and access logs; alarms on error rates
  • Redshift Data API and Athena API are data APIs you consume from code without managing drivers or servers

6Preparing Data for Transformation (skill 3.1.6)

  • AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual, no-code data preparation tool: datasets, profile jobs (statistics and quality), projects (interactive grid), recipes (ordered steps; over 250 prebuilt transformations), and recipe jobs (run on a schedule or on demand, write to S3 or other targets)
  • Typical steps: remove or fill nulls, standardize formats and case, split or merge columns, filter, mask or hash sensitive fields, join and union, change types
  • Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is an integrated workspace for data, analytics and AI: notebooks, visual ETL with Glue, SQL, catalog access and Amazon Q help, organized in domains and projects (Module 14)
  • Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler also prepares data visually for ML (Module 11)
Exam tip

"Analysts without coding skills clean and standardize data and run it on a schedule" → AWS Glue DataBrew.

7Querying Data with Amazon Athena (skill 3.1.7)

  • Athena is a serverless, interactive SQL query service over data in S3 (through the Glue Data Catalog); you pay for the data scanned, so partition, compress and use Parquet
  • Workgroups separate teams and workloads: per-workgroup query result location, encryption, data-scanned limits (cost control), query limits and CloudWatch metrics
  • Federated queries use Lambda-based data source connectors to query RDS, DynamoDB, Redshift, OpenSearch and on-premises sources in place
  • CTAS (CREATE TABLE AS SELECT) and INSERT INTO turn Athena into an ETL engine (convert to Parquet, partition, compact)
  • Views save queries; prepared statements and parameterized queries are reusable; query result reuse avoids re-running identical queries
  • Query timeout: about 30 minutes for SQL queries by default (adjustable) [Verify live]; results are written to S3
  • Athena notebooks with Apache Spark are in Module 11
Exam tip

"Control cost per team in Athena" → separate workgroups with data-scanned limits. "Query a database and S3 together without moving data" → Athena federated query.

8Lambda, Events and Schedulers (skills 3.1.8 and 3.1.9)

  • AWS Lambda automates glue steps: start a Glue job or crawler when a file arrives, validate or move files, call an API, fan out work, react to a CloudWatch alarm, clean up resources
  • Event-driven automation: S3 events, EventBridge rules, SQS, SNS, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis invoke Lambda (Modules 1 and 2)
  • EventBridge routes events and schedules work: rules with patterns, Pipes, and Scheduler (cron, rate, one-time, time zones, flexible windows) (Modules 1 and 4)
  • Operate it: dead-letter queues or destinations, retries, idempotent handlers, alarms on errors and throttles, reserved concurrency to protect downstream systems (Module 5)
  • Choose the trigger: time (Scheduler), event (EventBridge or S3), completion of a step (Step Functions, Glue triggers)
Exam tip

"Run a Glue job every night" → EventBridge Scheduler (or a Glue scheduled trigger); "run it when a file lands" → S3 event → EventBridge rule or Lambda.

9Exam Q&A

9.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1A new DAG file was uploaded to the S3 bucket of an Amazon MWAA environment but it does not appear in the Airflow UI. Where should the engineer look FIRST?

  • AThe Kinesis shard metrics for the environment's streams
  • BThe DAG processing logs in CloudWatch Logs, for syntax or import errors
  • CThe S3 Glacier restore status of the DAG bucket
  • DThe AWS Config rules that apply to the environment
Show the answer

Answer: B. DAG processing logs show parse errors; a missing DAG usually has a syntax or import error, or a missing requirement or plugin.

S2Airflow tasks stay in the queued state for a long time while the environment's workers are fully busy. What is the most direct fix?

  • AIncrease the size of the S3 bucket that holds the DAG files and the plugins
  • BDisable CloudWatch Logs to free capacity for the workers
  • CIncrease the maximum number of workers or the environment class
  • DChange the DAG schedule so that it runs every minute
Show the answer

Answer: C. Queued tasks mean there is not enough worker capacity; raising maximum workers or the environment class adds capacity.

S3A Lambda function starts an Amazon Athena query and must use the results. What is the correct pattern?

  • ACall StartQueryExecution, wait until the query succeeds, then call GetQueryResults
  • BCall GetQueryResults immediately after StartQueryExecution returns
  • CRead the results from a DynamoDB table that Athena fills
  • DUse Amazon Data Firehose to return the rows to the function
Show the answer

Answer: A. Athena queries run asynchronously: start the query, wait for success, then fetch the results (or use Step Functions with the Run a Job pattern).

S4Finance analysts with no coding skills need to clean and standardize CSV files and run the same steps every night. Which service fits?

  • AAWS Glue DataBrew with a recipe job on a schedule
  • BAmazon EMR with a Spark job written by the analysts
  • CAWS Lambda with a Python function for each step
  • DAmazon Kinesis Data Streams with a custom consumer
Show the answer

Answer: A. DataBrew provides visual preparation with reusable recipes and scheduled jobs for non-coders.

S5Two teams share an AWS account and Athena. The company wants a separate query result location and a monthly data-scanned limit for each team. What should be used?

  • AOne S3 bucket for all teams, with a separate folder for each team and a bucket policy
  • BA single IAM user that every team shares for queries
  • COne Athena workgroup per team, with its own result location and limits
  • DAmazon QuickSight datasets with one dataset for each team
Show the answer

Answer: C. Workgroups isolate query results, encryption settings and cost controls such as data-scanned limits per workload or team.

S6Which TWO practices make an automated pipeline easier to recover after a failure? (Select TWO.)

  • ARun all steps in a single function with no timeouts
  • BHard-code access keys in the code
  • CMake steps idempotent so they can be safely rerun
  • DAdd Retry and Catch handling with alarms that notify the team
  • ERemove all logging to save cost
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. Idempotent steps allow rerunning from the failed point, and retries, catches and alarms handle and surface failures.

10Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
MWAA troubleshooting CloudWatch scheduler/DAG-processing/worker logs; DAG missing = syntax/import/requirements; queued tasks = more workers; access = execution role; network = NAT/VPC endpoints
Step Functions troubleshooting Execution history and graph; States.TaskFailed, States.Timeout; IAM role for .sync/callback; Express logs in CloudWatch
Glue workflows Graph and job run logs; trigger must be activated; concurrency limits
SDK IAM roles, no hard-coded keys; auto retry with backoff; paginators, waiters, ClientToken; async data APIs (poll)
Service features EMR steps/auto-termination/scaling/Serverless; Redshift stored procedures, scheduled queries, auto-refresh MVs, zero-ETL; Glue triggers, bookmarks, auto scaling, Data Quality
API Gateway Stages, versions, throttling (10,000 rps default), usage plans, caching, authorizers, CloudWatch
DataBrew Visual, 250+ transforms, profile → recipe → job; SageMaker Unified Studio for notebooks and visual ETL
Athena Serverless SQL on S3, pay per data scanned, workgroups (limits), federated queries, CTAS/INSERT INTO, ~30 min timeout
Automation Lambda glue code; EventBridge rules and Scheduler; S3 events; DLQs, retries, idempotent handlers
